answer.verdict: Shipping path pumps posted keys about every 1 ms and presents on a 16.667 ms clock. Mode-select visual latency median fell from 29.83 ms (legacy poll) to 19.95 ms (paced). Fight seconds 50-139 stayed at median 60 fps. Present-on-tick was slower and is not the default. glReadPixels still costs about 2.2 ms.

Present readback is glReadPixels into frame.pixels when shared present is off. GSSharedPresent::Acquire has no caller. m_gs.init runs before InitWindow.
PCSX2 PrintWindow after keybd_event, n=8: 29.1 4.8 18.5 30.6 3.3 38.8 9.0 3.7 ms. Four are one poll and under 16.7 ms, so the hash is not a stable no-input control.

fix.change: atomic posted-key mask updated on the window thread; scePadRead samples it instead of waiting for the once-per-frame raylib poll

fast path: MsgWait 1 ms + PollInputEvents between presents; present on a 16.667 ms clock; SetTargetFPS(0) so the swap stamp is not the limiter sleep. TEKKEN4_INPUT_LEGACY=1 keeps the old poll and a post-stamp 16667 us sleep when logging.
paced unless TEKKEN4_INPUT_PRESENT=tick. Tick was measured slower (t4-t3 5.79 vs 2.24) and shifted the interlaced field.

contra: t2-t1 stays ~7.7 ms: that is the wait until the guest's next scePadRead (p95 16.28 ms, one frame). The host cannot cut it.

t5 median equals t4 because the block hash also changes between presses (0/24 held). Median visual time is the first present after the read, not a separate cursor detector. p95 t5 is 46.05 vs t4 31.21.
PCSX2 sub-frame hits are hash noise, not a game-latency number.
Fight second 50 was 46 frames; seconds 51-139 were 60 or 61.
